feed.headline: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees
feed.ai: The BBC's Dan Johnson travelled to the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus after evacuated Oleshky residents arrived in buses and ambulances following a temporary ceasefire.
feed.frag: Highlights the limits of national coordination

feed.headline: Iran delivers secret Khamenei message to Putin as Moscow pushes gas pipeline deal
feed.ai: Iran’s Security Council chief, Mohsen Rezaei, went to Moscow to deliver a personal message from Ayatollah Khamenei and discuss building a pipeline to import Russian gas.
feed.frag: Highlights the limits of national coordination

feed.headline: Azerbaijan and Ukraine forge new energy defence and trade agreements
feed.ai: An Azerbaijani delegation led by its energy minister travelled to Ukraine to sign a 2026-2027 Action Plan. Bilateral talks focused on emergency winter grid equipment, joint manufacturing, and expanding European transit via the Trans-Balkan route.

feed.headline: UK and EU agree draft deal to scrap Brexit red tape over food exports
feed.ai: The food deal, ahead of a UK-EU summit later this month, is the most significant part of the so-called Brexit reset agreed so far.
feed.frag: Highlights the limits of national coordination

feed.headline: Shock of rail tragedy gives way to sorrow and outrage in politically divided Spain
feed.ai: The latest train crash will pile pressure on the government of Pedro Sánchez, one month before the general election.

feed.headline: Europe Today: Democrats win Senate in rebuke of Trump as Poland’s constitutional crisis drags on
feed.ai: A blue wave has swept the US in the midterm elections, with Democrats winning the Senate and heading for a big House majority as votes are still being counted on the West Coast. We bring live analysis from Philadelphia and Brussels, plus Poland’s crisis, Ukraine talks and the EU enlargement race.

feed.headline: South Korea and Turkey sign financing pact as Seoul seeks role in planned nuclear power plant
feed.ai: Turkey and South Korea are expanding nuclear, defence and trade ties. Their latest agreement explores funding for nuclear projects, while Ankara weighs potential partners for its planned Sinop plant.
feed.frag: Highlights the limits of national coordination

feed.headline: Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster
feed.ai: Prosecutors begin investigating EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish railway line where a train crash killed 69 people.

feed.headline: 'We have proven ourselves': UAE vows to remain reliable energy supplier to Europe
feed.ai: One of the UAE's most senior energy officials told Euronews diversification has carried the country's energy sector through months of regional crisis, as Europe looks to the Gulf for secure supply.

feed.headline: Netherlands: Protesters storm Amsterdam data centre construction site
feed.ai: Protesters broke into a data centre construction site intended for Microsoft in Amsterdam, on 6 November, climbing cranes and unfurling banners denouncing artificial intelligence and the company's alleged involvement in the war in Gaza.

feed.headline: Spain: Zelensky urges Latin America to help repair Ukraine's power grid
feed.ai: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has appealed to Spain and Latin American countries for urgent help repairing Ukraine's damaged energy infrastructure. He also met King Felipe VI during the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid.

feed.headline: Milei and Sánchez exchange a cold greeting at Ibero-American Summit
feed.ai: Argentine President Javier Milei and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez exchanged a brief and frosty greeting at the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid on Wednesday. Their encounter comes two weeks after Milei called Sánchez an “unpresentable dictator”.
